## Western Africa Capitals
### Cabo Verde — Praia
Praia is the capital of Cabo Verde. The city lies on Santiago Island and serves as the political center of this Atlantic island state. Praia is one of Africa’s national capitals located on an island.

## Western Africa Capitals
### Côte d’Ivoire — Yamoussoukro
Yamoussoukro is the capital of Côte d’Ivoire. Abidjan is still the country’s leading commercial city and remains more visible in many business and travel contexts. The official capital designation belongs to Yamoussoukro.

## Western Africa Capitals
### Gambia — Banjul
Banjul is the capital of Gambia. It stands near the mouth of the Gambia River and reflects the country’s narrow river-based geography. The capital itself is relatively small compared with the wider Greater Banjul urban area.

## Western Africa Capitals
### Ghana — Accra
Accra is the capital of Ghana. It is a coastal capital on the Gulf of Guinea and one of the most widely recognized city names in West Africa. Accra also serves as a business, media, and diplomatic center. It became the capital of the British Gold Coast Colony in 1877 and retained that role after Ghana’s independence in 1957.

## Western Africa Capitals
### Guinea — Conakry
Conakry is the capital of Guinea. It is a coastal capital on the Atlantic side of West Africa. The city is the country’s main political and port center.

## Western Africa Capitals
### Guinea-Bissau — Bissau
Bissau is the capital of Guinea-Bissau. Neighboring Guinea is a separate country with its capital at Conakry, so the two similarly named states have different national capitals.

## Western Africa Capitals
### Liberia — Monrovia
Monrovia is the capital of Liberia. It is an Atlantic coastal city and the country’s main administrative center. It is also Liberia’s largest urban center and principal port city.

## Western Africa Capitals
### Mali — Bamako
Bamako is the capital of Mali. It lies on the Niger River and serves as the country’s main political and urban center. Its inland position along the river has influenced its development as a transport and commercial center.

## Western Africa Capitals
### Mauritania — Nouakchott
Nouakchott is the capital of Mauritania. It is a coastal city on the Atlantic edge of the Sahara and functions as the country’s main political and administrative center.

## Western Africa Capitals
### Niger — Niamey
Niamey is the capital of Niger and stands on the Niger River. Neighboring Nigeria is a separate country whose capital is Abuja.

## Western Africa Capitals
### Nigeria — Abuja
Abuja is the capital of Nigeria. The city was chosen as a federal capital in a central location rather than keeping the capital in Lagos. Abuja formally became the capital in December 1991 and remains the seat of Nigeria’s federal government.

## Western Africa Capitals
### Senegal — Dakar
Dakar is the capital of Senegal. It sits on the Cap-Vert Peninsula and is one of the major Atlantic capitals in Africa. Its far-west coastal location makes it geographically distinctive.

## Western Africa Capitals
### Sierra Leone — Freetown
Freetown is the capital of Sierra Leone. It is a coastal capital with a deep harbor and remains the country’s central administrative city.

## Western Africa Capitals
### Togo — Lomé
Lomé is the capital of Togo. It is a coastal city on the Gulf of Guinea and an active national port. Its position near the border with Ghana connects the capital with regional coastal trade routes.

## Middle Africa Capitals
Middle Africa includes nine countries in the UN grouping used here. The subregion contains some of the continent’s major river capitals and the mainland capital designated by Equatorial Guinea in 2026.

## Middle Africa Capitals
### Angola — Luanda
Luanda is the capital of Angola. It is a large Atlantic capital and one of the biggest urban centers on Africa’s western coast, concentrating national government, port activity, and a large share of the country’s urban population.

## Middle Africa Capitals
### Cameroon — Yaoundé
Yaoundé is the capital of Cameroon. Douala is the country’s larger port and business city, so Cameroon separates its national political center from its leading commercial metropolis.

## Middle Africa Capitals
### Central African Republic — Bangui
Bangui is the capital of the Central African Republic. It lies on the Ubangi River and serves as the country’s main political center.

## Middle Africa Capitals
### Chad — N’Djamena
N’Djamena is the capital of Chad. It stands near the confluence of the Chari and Logone rivers in the western part of the country, close to the border with Cameroon.

## Middle Africa Capitals
### Republic of the Congo — Brazzaville
Brazzaville is the capital of the Republic of the Congo. The city sits on the north bank of the Congo River directly across from Kinshasa, the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

## Middle Africa Capitals
### Democratic Republic of the Congo — Kinshasa
Kinshasa is the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It is one of Africa’s largest urban capitals and occupies the south bank of the Congo River directly opposite Brazzaville.

## Middle Africa Capitals
### Equatorial Guinea — Ciudad de la Paz
**Ciudad de la Paz is the capital designated by Equatorial Guinea in 2026.** It replaced Malabo in the official capital designation on 2 January 2026, when Decree Law No. 1/2026 declared the planned mainland city the national capital.
Ciudad de la Paz is in Djibloho Province in the Río Muni continental region. Malabo remains the principal city on Bioko Island. The transfer of national institutions is being implemented separately from the legal declaration.

## Middle Africa Capitals
### Gabon — Libreville
Libreville is the capital of Gabon. It is an Atlantic coastal capital and the country’s main political center. Libreville is also an important administrative and commercial city in Central Africa.

## Middle Africa Capitals
### São Tomé and Príncipe — São Tomé
São Tomé is the capital of São Tomé and Príncipe. The city shares its name with the country’s largest island and serves as the principal political and administrative center of this island state in the Gulf of Guinea.

## Eastern Africa Capitals
Eastern Africa has 18 countries in this list, the highest subregional count. Its capitals include highland cities, island capitals, diplomatic centers, and several capitals that are often confused with older or larger urban centers.

## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Burundi — Gitega
Gitega is the political capital of Burundi. Bujumbura was the former political capital and remains the country’s largest city and economic capital. Burundi’s government distinguishes the functions of the two cities.

## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Comoros — Moroni
Moroni is the capital of Comoros. It is located on Grande Comore, also known as Ngazidja, and functions as the political center of this island state in the Indian Ocean.

## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Djibouti — Djibouti
Djibouti is the capital of Djibouti. The city and country share the same name. It is also an important port city on the Horn of Africa, situated near the Gulf of Aden.

## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Eritrea — Asmara
Asmara is the capital of Eritrea. Although Eritrea has a long Red Sea coastline, the capital is inland in the Eritrean highlands at an elevation of more than 2,000 meters.

## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Ethiopia — Addis Ababa
Addis Ababa is the capital of Ethiopia and a major diplomatic center. It hosts the headquarters of the African Union and the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa, giving the city a continental and international role alongside its national government functions.

## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Kenya — Nairobi
Nairobi is the capital of Kenya. It is a large inland city in the highlands and one of Africa’s major international centers. Nairobi also hosts United Nations offices, including the headquarters of UNEP and UN-Habitat.

## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Madagascar — Antananarivo
Antananarivo is the capital of Madagascar. It sits in the central highlands rather than on the coast. Although Madagascar is an island country, its national capital is inland.

## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Malawi — Lilongwe
Lilongwe is the capital of Malawi. It serves as the administrative center, while Blantyre remains a major commercial city. The country’s capital and leading business city therefore have different roles.

## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Mauritius — Port Louis
Port Louis is the capital of Mauritius. The city is a port and the political and commercial center of the island state in the Indian Ocean.

## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Mozambique — Maputo
Maputo is the capital of Mozambique. It lies on the coast in the far south of the country and serves as the national political center and a major port. Its position is farther south than many of Mozambique’s northern and central population centers.

## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Rwanda — Kigali
Kigali is the capital of Rwanda. It is centrally located within the country and functions as the main administrative and service center.

## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Seychelles — Victoria
Victoria is the capital of Seychelles. It is located on Mahé and is one of the smaller national capitals in Africa. The city is the principal political and administrative center of the island state.

## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Somalia — Mogadishu
Mogadishu is the capital of Somalia. It is a coastal capital on the Indian Ocean and the country’s main port city. It also houses the country’s federal government institutions.

## Eastern Africa Capitals
### South Sudan — Juba
Juba is the capital of South Sudan and is located on the White Nile. Khartoum is the capital of neighboring Sudan, so the two states have distinct national capitals despite their shared history before South Sudan became independent in 2011.

## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Tanzania — Dodoma
Dodoma is the capital of Tanzania. Dar es Salaam remains the country’s largest city, principal port, and leading commercial center, which is why the former capital still appears prominently in older material and general references.

## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Uganda — Kampala
Kampala is the capital of Uganda. It lies in the country’s central region near Lake Victoria and serves as the main political and urban center, with government, business, education, and transport functions concentrated across the wider metropolitan area.

## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Zambia — Lusaka
Lusaka is the capital of Zambia. It is an inland city on the south-central plateau and the country’s leading administrative center, connected by major road corridors to other parts of Zambia and the wider Southern African region.

## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Zimbabwe — Harare
Harare is the capital of Zimbabwe. It is the country’s largest city and main administrative center. The capital and largest city are the same in this case.

## Southern Africa Capitals
Southern Africa has five countries in this UN grouping. The subregion includes South Africa’s three-capital arrangement, Eswatini’s division between Mbabane and Lobamba, and several inland capitals located near major national or cross-border transport corridors.

## Southern Africa Capitals
### Botswana — Gaborone
Gaborone is the capital of Botswana. It lies close to the border with South Africa and serves as the country’s political and administrative center. Gaborone developed as a modern administrative city following Botswana’s independence in 1966.

## Southern Africa Capitals
### Eswatini — Mbabane and Lobamba
Mbabane is the administrative capital of Eswatini, while Lobamba holds royal and legislative functions. Both cities are identified in descriptions of the country’s government. For a basic capital table, Mbabane is commonly listed first, with Lobamba included as the second capital.

## Southern Africa Capitals
### Lesotho — Maseru
Maseru is the capital of Lesotho. It lies near the border with South Africa and serves as the country’s main political and urban center. Lesotho is entirely surrounded by South African territory.

## Southern Africa Capitals
### Namibia — Windhoek
Windhoek is the capital of Namibia. It is centrally placed and functions as the main administrative center in a large, sparsely populated country.

## Southern Africa Capitals
### South Africa — Pretoria, Cape Town, and Bloemfontein
Pretoria is South Africa’s administrative capital, Cape Town is the legislative capital, and Bloemfontein is the judicial capital in the terminology used by the South African government. The Constitutional Court is located in Johannesburg, while the Supreme Court of Appeal is in Bloemfontein.

## Geographic and Functional Patterns Among African Capitals
African capitals can be compared by geography, government function, and naming pattern. Coastal, inland, island, and multi-city capital arrangements show how different national political centers can be across the continent.

## Geographic and Functional Patterns Among African Capitals
### Coastal Capitals
Many African capitals lie on or near the coast. Examples include Algiers, Tripoli, Tunis, Rabat, Accra, Conakry, Monrovia, Dakar, Lomé, Luanda, Libreville, Djibouti, Mogadishu, Maputo, Port Louis, Victoria, and Praia. Coastal capitals often grew around ports, trade routes, or older administrative centers connected to sea access.

## Geographic and Functional Patterns Among African Capitals
### Inland Capitals
A large group of capitals are inland political centers rather than seaports. Abuja, Bamako, Niamey, Ouagadougou, Yaoundé, Bangui, Kigali, Kampala, Lusaka, Harare, Windhoek, Gaborone, Addis Ababa, Asmara, Antananarivo, and Dodoma all fit this pattern. Inland capitals often sit closer to the national interior or along older land routes and plateaus.

## Geographic and Functional Patterns Among African Capitals
### Island Capitals
The sovereign island-state capitals in this 54-country list are Praia in Cabo Verde, Moroni in Comoros, Port Louis in Mauritius, Victoria in Seychelles, and São Tomé in São Tomé and Príncipe.
Equatorial Guinea is not part of this island-capital group under its 2026 capital designation: Ciudad de la Paz is on the mainland in Djibloho Province, while its former capital, Malabo, is located on Bioko Island.

## Geographic and Functional Patterns Among African Capitals
### Capitals That Are Not the Largest City
Several African capitals do not dominate their country by population or business activity. Porto-Novo, Yamoussoukro, Dodoma, Gitega, Lilongwe, Yaoundé, Mbabane, and Pretoria show that capital status is a legal or administrative function rather than a measure of urban size.

## Geographic and Functional Patterns Among African Capitals
### Country Names Often Confused With Each Other
*   **Niger — Niamey** and **Nigeria — Abuja**  
*   **Republic of the Congo — Brazzaville** and **Democratic Republic of the Congo — Kinshasa**  
*   **Guinea — Conakry** and **Guinea-Bissau — Bissau**  
*   **Sudan — Khartoum** and **South Sudan — Juba**
These country names are easy to confuse because several are geographically close or linguistically similar. Their capitals provide a clear distinction between the separate states.

## Common Questions About African Capitals
### What Is the Capital of Africa?
**Africa does not have a single capital city because Africa is a continent, not a country.** It contains 54 independent countries that are members of the United Nations, each with its own national capital arrangement.
**Addis Ababa, Ethiopia,** is sometimes informally described as Africa’s diplomatic capital because it hosts the headquarters of the African Union and the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa. However, Addis Ababa is officially the capital of Ethiopia, not the capital of the African continent.

## Common Questions About African Capitals
### How Many Countries Are in Africa?
This list contains Africa’s **54 United Nations member states**. The African Union has 55 members because it also includes the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic. The 54-country total used here follows the UN-member-state scope.

## Common Questions About African Capitals
### What Is the Capital of South Africa?
South Africa has three capitals with different national functions: **Pretoria** is the administrative capital, **Cape Town** is the legislative capital, and **Bloemfontein** is the judicial capital in South African government terminology. The Constitutional Court is in Johannesburg.

## Common Questions About African Capitals
### Is Abidjan the Capital of Côte d’Ivoire?
No. Yamoussoukro is the official capital. Abidjan is the country’s leading commercial city and hosts many national government and diplomatic functions.

## Common Questions About African Capitals
### Is Cotonou the Capital of Benin?
No. Porto-Novo is the official capital of Benin. Cotonou is the larger economic center and principal seat of government activity.

## Common Questions About African Capitals
### What Is the Current Capital of Burundi?
Gitega is the political capital of Burundi. Bujumbura was the former political capital and remains the country’s economic capital and largest city. Both cities have different national functions.

## Common Questions About African Capitals
### What Is the Capital of Equatorial Guinea?
Ciudad de la Paz was designated the capital of Equatorial Guinea on 2 January 2026 under Decree Law No. 1/2026. Malabo was the previous capital. The transfer of government institutions to the mainland city is being carried out separately from the legal designation.

## Common Questions About African Capitals
### Are All African Capitals the Biggest City in the Country?
No. Several are not. Abuja is not Nigeria’s largest city. Dodoma is not Tanzania’s largest city. Yamoussoukro is not Côte d’Ivoire’s largest city. Porto-Novo is not Benin’s largest city. Capital status and city size are separate characteristics.

## Common Questions About African Capitals
### Which African Capitals Have Strong Diplomatic Roles?
Addis Ababa and Nairobi are particularly prominent. Addis Ababa hosts the African Union headquarters. Nairobi hosts the United Nations Office at Nairobi, along with UNEP and UN-Habitat headquarters.

## Common Questions About African Capitals
### Which African Capitals Are on Islands?
Praia, Moroni, Port Louis, Victoria, and São Tomé are the national capitals of Africa’s sovereign island states in this 54-country list. Ciudad de la Paz in Equatorial Guinea is on the African mainland, although the country also includes the island of Bioko, where the former capital Malabo is located.

## Common Questions About African Capitals
### Which African Capital Cities Face Each Other Across a River?
**Brazzaville and Kinshasa** face each other across the Congo River. They belong to different countries: the Republic of the Congo and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

*   United Nations — World Population Prospects 2024 (population estimates and geographic definitions).  
*   United Nations — Population and Vital Statistics Report, January 2026 (mid-year 2024 population estimates by African subregion).  
*   African Union — About the African Union (membership and continental organization).  
*   Government of South Africa — South Africa’s Provinces and Capitals (Pretoria, Cape Town, and Bloemfontein).

*   Government of Burundi — National Overview (Gitega as political capital and Bujumbura as economic capital).

Freetown is the capital of Sierra Leone. It is a coastal capital with a deep harbor and remains the country’s central administrative city.
texts.50:
## Western Africa Capitals
### Togo — Lomé
Lomé is the capital of Togo. It is a coastal city on the Gulf of Guinea and an active national port. Its position near the border with Ghana connects the capital with regional coastal trade routes.
texts.51:
## Middle Africa Capitals
Middle Africa includes nine countries in the UN grouping used here. The subregion contains some of the continent’s major river capitals and the mainland capital designated by Equatorial Guinea in 2026.
texts.52:
## Middle Africa Capitals
### Angola — Luanda
Luanda is the capital of Angola. It is a large Atlantic capital and one of the biggest urban centers on Africa’s western coast, concentrating national government, port activity, and a large share of the country’s urban population.
texts.53:
## Middle Africa Capitals
### Cameroon — Yaoundé
Yaoundé is the capital of Cameroon. Douala is the country’s larger port and business city, so Cameroon separates its national political center from its leading commercial metropolis.
texts.54:
## Middle Africa Capitals
### Central African Republic — Bangui
Bangui is the capital of the Central African Republic. It lies on the Ubangi River and serves as the country’s main political center.
texts.55:
## Middle Africa Capitals
### Chad — N’Djamena
N’Djamena is the capital of Chad. It stands near the confluence of the Chari and Logone rivers in the western part of the country, close to the border with Cameroon.
texts.56:
## Middle Africa Capitals
### Republic of the Congo — Brazzaville
Brazzaville is the capital of the Republic of the Congo. The city sits on the north bank of the Congo River directly across from Kinshasa, the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
texts.57:
## Middle Africa Capitals
### Democratic Republic of the Congo — Kinshasa
Kinshasa is the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It is one of Africa’s largest urban capitals and occupies the south bank of the Congo River directly opposite Brazzaville.
texts.58:
## Middle Africa Capitals
### Equatorial Guinea — Ciudad de la Paz
**Ciudad de la Paz is the capital designated by Equatorial Guinea in 2026.** It replaced Malabo in the official capital designation on 2 January 2026, when Decree Law No. 1/2026 declared the planned mainland city the national capital.
Ciudad de la Paz is in Djibloho Province in the Río Muni continental region. Malabo remains the principal city on Bioko Island. The transfer of national institutions is being implemented separately from the legal declaration.
texts.59:
## Middle Africa Capitals
### Gabon — Libreville
Libreville is the capital of Gabon. It is an Atlantic coastal capital and the country’s main political center. Libreville is also an important administrative and commercial city in Central Africa.
texts.60:
## Middle Africa Capitals
### São Tomé and Príncipe — São Tomé
São Tomé is the capital of São Tomé and Príncipe. The city shares its name with the country’s largest island and serves as the principal political and administrative center of this island state in the Gulf of Guinea.
texts.61:
## Eastern Africa Capitals
Eastern Africa has 18 countries in this list, the highest subregional count. Its capitals include highland cities, island capitals, diplomatic centers, and several capitals that are often confused with older or larger urban centers.
texts.62:
## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Burundi — Gitega
Gitega is the political capital of Burundi. Bujumbura was the former political capital and remains the country’s largest city and economic capital. Burundi’s government distinguishes the functions of the two cities.
texts.63:
## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Comoros — Moroni
Moroni is the capital of Comoros. It is located on Grande Comore, also known as Ngazidja, and functions as the political center of this island state in the Indian Ocean.
texts.64:
## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Djibouti — Djibouti
Djibouti is the capital of Djibouti. The city and country share the same name. It is also an important port city on the Horn of Africa, situated near the Gulf of Aden.
texts.65:
## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Eritrea — Asmara
Asmara is the capital of Eritrea. Although Eritrea has a long Red Sea coastline, the capital is inland in the Eritrean highlands at an elevation of more than 2,000 meters.
texts.66:
## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Ethiopia — Addis Ababa
Addis Ababa is the capital of Ethiopia and a major diplomatic center. It hosts the headquarters of the African Union and the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa, giving the city a continental and international role alongside its national government functions.
texts.67:
## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Kenya — Nairobi
Nairobi is the capital of Kenya. It is a large inland city in the highlands and one of Africa’s major international centers. Nairobi also hosts United Nations offices, including the headquarters of UNEP and UN-Habitat.
texts.68:
## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Madagascar — Antananarivo
Antananarivo is the capital of Madagascar. It sits in the central highlands rather than on the coast. Although Madagascar is an island country, its national capital is inland.
texts.69:
## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Malawi — Lilongwe
Lilongwe is the capital of Malawi. It serves as the administrative center, while Blantyre remains a major commercial city. The country’s capital and leading business city therefore have different roles.
texts.70:
## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Mauritius — Port Louis
Port Louis is the capital of Mauritius. The city is a port and the political and commercial center of the island state in the Indian Ocean.
texts.71:
## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Mozambique — Maputo
Maputo is the capital of Mozambique. It lies on the coast in the far south of the country and serves as the national political center and a major port. Its position is farther south than many of Mozambique’s northern and central population centers.
texts.72:
## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Rwanda — Kigali
Kigali is the capital of Rwanda. It is centrally located within the country and functions as the main administrative and service center.
texts.73:
## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Seychelles — Victoria
Victoria is the capital of Seychelles. It is located on Mahé and is one of the smaller national capitals in Africa. The city is the principal political and administrative center of the island state.
texts.74:
## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Somalia — Mogadishu
Mogadishu is the capital of Somalia. It is a coastal capital on the Indian Ocean and the country’s main port city. It also houses the country’s federal government institutions.
texts.75:
## Eastern Africa Capitals
### South Sudan — Juba
Juba is the capital of South Sudan and is located on the White Nile. Khartoum is the capital of neighboring Sudan, so the two states have distinct national capitals despite their shared history before South Sudan became independent in 2011.
texts.76:
## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Tanzania — Dodoma
Dodoma is the capital of Tanzania. Dar es Salaam remains the country’s largest city, principal port, and leading commercial center, which is why the former capital still appears prominently in older material and general references.
texts.77:
## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Uganda — Kampala
Kampala is the capital of Uganda. It lies in the country’s central region near Lake Victoria and serves as the main political and urban center, with government, business, education, and transport functions concentrated across the wider metropolitan area.
texts.78:
## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Zambia — Lusaka
Lusaka is the capital of Zambia. It is an inland city on the south-central plateau and the country’s leading administrative center, connected by major road corridors to other parts of Zambia and the wider Southern African region.
texts.79:
## Eastern Africa Capitals
### Zimbabwe — Harare
Harare is the capital of Zimbabwe. It is the country’s largest city and main administrative center. The capital and largest city are the same in this case.
texts.80:
## Southern Africa Capitals
Southern Africa has five countries in this UN grouping. The subregion includes South Africa’s three-capital arrangement, Eswatini’s division between Mbabane and Lobamba, and several inland capitals located near major national or cross-border transport corridors.
texts.81:
## Southern Africa Capitals
### Botswana — Gaborone
Gaborone is the capital of Botswana. It lies close to the border with South Africa and serves as the country’s political and administrative center. Gaborone developed as a modern administrative city following Botswana’s independence in 1966.
texts.82:
## Southern Africa Capitals
### Eswatini — Mbabane and Lobamba
Mbabane is the administrative capital of Eswatini, while Lobamba holds royal and legislative functions. Both cities are identified in descriptions of the country’s government. For a basic capital table, Mbabane is commonly listed first, with Lobamba included as the second capital.
texts.83:
## Southern Africa Capitals
### Lesotho — Maseru
Maseru is the capital of Lesotho. It lies near the border with South Africa and serves as the country’s main political and urban center. Lesotho is entirely surrounded by South African territory.
texts.84:
## Southern Africa Capitals
### Namibia — Windhoek
Windhoek is the capital of Namibia. It is centrally placed and functions as the main administrative center in a large, sparsely populated country.
texts.85:
## Southern Africa Capitals
### South Africa — Pretoria, Cape Town, and Bloemfontein
Pretoria is South Africa’s administrative capital, Cape Town is the legislative capital, and Bloemfontein is the judicial capital in the terminology used by the South African government. The Constitutional Court is located in Johannesburg, while the Supreme Court of Appeal is in Bloemfontein.
texts.86:
## Geographic and Functional Patterns Among African Capitals
African capitals can be compared by geography, government function, and naming pattern. Coastal, inland, island, and multi-city capital arrangements show how different national political centers can be across the continent.
texts.87:
## Geographic and Functional Patterns Among African Capitals
### Coastal Capitals
Many African capitals lie on or near the coast. Examples include Algiers, Tripoli, Tunis, Rabat, Accra, Conakry, Monrovia, Dakar, Lomé, Luanda, Libreville, Djibouti, Mogadishu, Maputo, Port Louis, Victoria, and Praia. Coastal capitals often grew around ports, trade routes, or older administrative centers connected to sea access.
texts.88:
## Geographic and Functional Patterns Among African Capitals
### Inland Capitals
A large group of capitals are inland political centers rather than seaports. Abuja, Bamako, Niamey, Ouagadougou, Yaoundé, Bangui, Kigali, Kampala, Lusaka, Harare, Windhoek, Gaborone, Addis Ababa, Asmara, Antananarivo, and Dodoma all fit this pattern. Inland capitals often sit closer to the national interior or along older land routes and plateaus.
texts.89:
## Geographic and Functional Patterns Among African Capitals
### Island Capitals
The sovereign island-state capitals in this 54-country list are Praia in Cabo Verde, Moroni in Comoros, Port Louis in Mauritius, Victoria in Seychelles, and São Tomé in São Tomé and Príncipe.
Equatorial Guinea is not part of this island-capital group under its 2026 capital designation: Ciudad de la Paz is on the mainland in Djibloho Province, while its former capital, Malabo, is located on Bioko Island.
texts.90:
## Geographic and Functional Patterns Among African Capitals
### Capitals That Are Not the Largest City
Several African capitals do not dominate their country by population or business activity. Porto-Novo, Yamoussoukro, Dodoma, Gitega, Lilongwe, Yaoundé, Mbabane, and Pretoria show that capital status is a legal or administrative function rather than a measure of urban size.
texts.91:
## Geographic and Functional Patterns Among African Capitals
### Country Names Often Confused With Each Other
*   **Niger — Niamey** and **Nigeria — Abuja**  
*   **Republic of the Congo — Brazzaville** and **Democratic Republic of the Congo — Kinshasa**  
*   **Guinea — Conakry** and **Guinea-Bissau — Bissau**  
*   **Sudan — Khartoum** and **South Sudan — Juba**
These country names are easy to confuse because several are geographically close or linguistically similar. Their capitals provide a clear distinction between the separate states.
texts.92:
## Common Questions About African Capitals
### What Is the Capital of Africa?
**Africa does not have a single capital city because Africa is a continent, not a country.** It contains 54 independent countries that are members of the United Nations, each with its own national capital arrangement.
**Addis Ababa, Ethiopia,** is sometimes informally described as Africa’s diplomatic capital because it hosts the headquarters of the African Union and the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa. However, Addis Ababa is officially the capital of Ethiopia, not the capital of the African continent.
texts.93:
## Common Questions About African Capitals
### How Many Countries Are in Africa?
This list contains Africa’s **54 United Nations member states**. The African Union has 55 members because it also includes the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic. The 54-country total used here follows the UN-member-state scope.
texts.94:
## Common Questions About African Capitals
### What Is the Capital of South Africa?
South Africa has three capitals with different national functions: **Pretoria** is the administrative capital, **Cape Town** is the legislative capital, and **Bloemfontein** is the judicial capital in South African government terminology. The Constitutional Court is in Johannesburg.
texts.95:
## Common Questions About African Capitals
### Is Abidjan the Capital of Côte d’Ivoire?
No. Yamoussoukro is the official capital. Abidjan is the country’s leading commercial city and hosts many national government and diplomatic functions.
texts.96:
## Common Questions About African Capitals
### Is Cotonou the Capital of Benin?
No. Porto-Novo is the official capital of Benin. Cotonou is the larger economic center and principal seat of government activity.
texts.97:
## Common Questions About African Capitals
### What Is the Current Capital of Burundi?
Gitega is the political capital of Burundi. Bujumbura was the former political capital and remains the country’s economic capital and largest city. Both cities have different national functions.
texts.98:
## Common Questions About African Capitals
### What Is the Capital of Equatorial Guinea?
Ciudad de la Paz was designated the capital of Equatorial Guinea on 2 January 2026 under Decree Law No. 1/2026. Malabo was the previous capital. The transfer of government institutions to the mainland city is being carried out separately from the legal designation.
texts.99:
## Common Questions About African Capitals
### Are All African Capitals the Biggest City in the Country?
No. Several are not. Abuja is not Nigeria’s largest city. Dodoma is not Tanzania’s largest city. Yamoussoukro is not Côte d’Ivoire’s largest city. Porto-Novo is not Benin’s largest city. Capital status and city size are separate characteristics.
texts.100:
## Common Questions About African Capitals
### Which African Capitals Have Strong Diplomatic Roles?
Addis Ababa and Nairobi are particularly prominent. Addis Ababa hosts the African Union headquarters. Nairobi hosts the United Nations Office at Nairobi, along with UNEP and UN-Habitat headquarters.
texts.101:
## Common Questions About African Capitals
### Which African Capitals Are on Islands?
Praia, Moroni, Port Louis, Victoria, and São Tomé are the national capitals of Africa’s sovereign island states in this 54-country list. Ciudad de la Paz in Equatorial Guinea is on the African mainland, although the country also includes the island of Bioko, where the former capital Malabo is located.
texts.102:
## Common Questions About African Capitals
### Which African Capital Cities Face Each Other Across a River?
**Brazzaville and Kinshasa** face each other across the Congo River. They belong to different countries: the Republic of the Congo and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
texts.103:

# ICC announces schedule for Pepsi ICC World Cricket League Division 4
6 April, 2010
The ICC today announced the schedule for the Pepsi ICC World Cricket League Division 4 in Dar Es Salaam, Tanzania
The event, which will take place from 4-11 October, will see six teams attempt to take the next step on the road to the ICC Cricket World Cup 2011.
Afghanistan and Jersey, who progressed from the Pepsi ICC World Cricket League Division 5 event, will face a tough challenge if they are to finish in the top two qualifying spots as they face Hong Kong, who won the ACC Trophy Elite 2008, Italy, who recorded a win over Netherlands at the ICC European Division 1 Championship earlier this year, Fiji and hosts Tanzania.
The top two sides will qualify for the Pepsi ICC World Cricket League Division 3 in Argentina in January, with the top two sides from that event, completing the line-up for the 12-team ICC Cricket World Cup Qualifier which is scheduled to take place in April 2009.
The four leading sides at that event will make it to the ICC Cricket World Cup 2011 which is being held in Bangladesh, India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
Squad announcements for the Dar Es Salaam event will be released to media on the WCL Div. 4 distribution list in due course (see below for details on how to be included on this list).
**Pepsi ICC World Cricket League Division 4 Tournament Schedule**
Thursday 2 October – Opening Ceremony
Saturday 4 October – Hong Kong v Italy (University), Tanzania v Jersey (Anadil Burhani), Fiji v Afghanistan (Leaders Club Kinondoni)
Sunday 5 October – Afghanistan v Jersey (University), Italy v Fiji (Anadil Burhani), Hong Kong v Tanzania (Leaders Club Kinondoni)
Monday 6 October – Rest day
Tuesday 7 October – Hong Kong v Fiji (University), Tanzania v Afghanistan (Anadil Burhani), Italy v Jersey (Leaders Club Kinondoni)
Wednesday 8 October – Italy v Tanzania (University), Hong Kong v Afghanistan (Anadil Burhani), Fiji v Jersey (Leaders Club Kinondoni)
Thursday 9 October – Rest day
Saturday 10 October – Fiji v Tanzania (University), Hong Kong v Jersey (Anadil Burhani), Italy v Afghanistan (Leaders Club Kinondoni)

**David Odhiambo** (born 27 April 1976) is a Kenyan cricket umpire. As of April 2023, he has stood in nine One Day International (ODIs), 31 Twenty20 Internationals (T20Is), one women's ODI and four women's T20I matches.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Odhiambo#cite_note-Cricinfo-1)
He was one of the seventeen on-field umpires for the 2018 Under-19 Cricket World Cup, held in New Zealand.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Odhiambo#cite_note-2018U19-2) He was named as one of the eight on-field umpires for the 2019 ICC World Cricket League Division Two tournament in Namibia.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Odhiambo#cite_note-3)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
This is a list of cricket umpires who have officiated in at least one men's Twenty20 International (T20I) match. As of November 2026, at least 598 umpires have officiated in a men's T20I match.[1][a]
On 20 January 2019, Qatar's Shivani Mishra became the first female on-field umpire to officiate in a men's T20I when she stood in a match in the ACC Western Region T20 tournament.[2]
In November 2020, in the second T20I between Pakistan and Zimbabwe, Pakistan's Ahsan Raza stood in his 50th men's T20I match as an on-field umpire, becoming the first umpire to reach the milestone in the format.[3]
On 5 April 2023, New Zealand's Kim Cotton stood in her first men's T20I match between New Zealand and Sri Lanka when Sri Lanka toured New Zealand.[4] She became the first female to officiate in a men's T20I between full members as an on-field umpire.[5]
On 13 December 2025, during the men's T20 event in the 2025 Southeast Asian Games, Malaysia's Viswanadan Kalidas became the first umpire to officiate in 100 men's T20I matches.[6]

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
This is a list of cricket umpires who have officiated in at least one men's Twenty20 International (T20I) match. As of November 2026, at least 598 umpires have officiated in a men's T20I match.[1][a]
On 20 January 2019, Qatar's Shivani Mishra became the first female on-field umpire to officiate in a men's T20I when she stood in a match in the ACC Western Region T20 tournament.[2]
In November 2020, in the second T20I between Pakistan and Zimbabwe, Pakistan's Ahsan Raza stood in his 50th men's T20I match as an on-field umpire, becoming the first umpire to reach the milestone in the format.[3]
On 5 April 2023, New Zealand's Kim Cotton stood in her first men's T20I match between New Zealand and Sri Lanka when Sri Lanka toured New Zealand.[4] She became the first female to officiate in a men's T20I between full members as an on-field umpire.[5]
On 13 December 2025, during the men's T20 event in the 2025 Southeast Asian Games, Malaysia's Viswanadan Kalidas became the first umpire to officiate in 100 men's T20I matches.[6]

**David Odhiambo** (born 27 April 1976) is a Kenyan cricket umpire. As of April 2023, he has stood in nine One Day International (ODIs), 31 Twenty20 Internationals (T20Is), one women's ODI and four women's T20I matches.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Odhiambo#cite_note-Cricinfo-1)
He was one of the seventeen on-field umpires for the 2018 Under-19 Cricket World Cup, held in New Zealand.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Odhiambo#cite_note-2018U19-2) He was named as one of the eight on-field umpires for the 2019 ICC World Cricket League Division Two tournament in Namibia.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Odhiambo#cite_note-3)

# Africa trek to World T20 begins in Lagos
Cricket365 14 Apr 2018
[](whatsapp://send/?text=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.cricket365.com%2Flatest-news%2Fafrica-trek-to-world-t20-begins-in-lagos)
**Nigeria is all set for action on Saturday, 14 April, as the ICC World Twenty20 Africa Qualifier A begins in Lagos.**
The Ghanaian side will be led by the experienced Peter Ananya, who will also be looking to provide some stability with the bat. Ananya’s team also includes the Ateak brothers, Simon and Samson, who have also turned out at this level before.
Sierra Leone come into the tournament looking to cause an upset, will have to build on their latest performance. They took on the might of Tanzania a year ago in their last fixture of real significance.
Also looking to make a play is The Gambia, who will look to the vastly experienced Dumbuya Mbye, who has been plying his trade at this level for over a decade. The right-hand batsman, who also bowls useful medium pace and off-spin, has seen it all before, and knows he will have to enjoy a good week in Lagos.
Finally, Nigeria will enjoy plenty of hometown support over the next week, as they look to progress to the next stage of qualification for the ICC WorldT20, Australia 2020.
The men in green will be led again by Chimezie Onwuzulike, whose all-round skills are vital to the cause. He will lead a young, energetic side, and they are charged with making it a week to remember on home soil.
Fixtures:

9:30am Nigeria vs Sierra Leone
1:50pm Ghana vs The Gambia

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
The **2018–19 ICC T20 World Cup Africa Qualifier** was a tournament played as part of qualification process for the 2021 ICC T20 World Cup.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-1)
Twelve regional qualifiers for the 2021 World Cup were held by the International Cricket Council (ICC), with 62 teams[[n 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Teams-2) competing during 2018 in five regions – Africa (3 groups), Americas (2), Asia (2), East Asia Pacific (2) and Europe (3). The top 25 sides from these progressed to five Regional Finals in 2019, with seven teams then going on to compete in the 2019 ICC T20 World Cup Qualifier,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-pressrelase-3)[[n 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-UAE=sr-4) along with the six lowest ranked sides from the ICC T20I Championship.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-pressrelase-3)

The first African sub-regional qualifier (North-Western sub region) was held in Nigeria, with the two other groups staged in Botswana and Rwanda.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Road_to_2020-5)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Africa_sub_region-6) The top two teams in each group advanced to the regional finals tournament, which will determine two African entrants to the 2019 ICC T20 World Cup Qualifier. In April 2018, the International Cricket Council (ICC) granted full international status to Twenty20 men's matches played between member sides from 1 January 2019 onwards. Therefore, all the matches in the Regional Finals were played as Twenty20 Internationals (T20Is).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-status-7)

From the North-Western sub region group, both Ghana and Nigeria qualified for the Africa Regional Finals.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-GhaNgr-8)Simon Ateak of Ghana was named the player of the tournament in the North-Western group.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-9) The second group, the Eastern sub region, started on 7 July 2018.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-10) Both Kenya and Uganda qualified for the Africa Regional Finals from the Eastern sub region group.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Kenya-11)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Uganda-12) Uganda's Riazat Ali Shah was named the player of the tournament for the Eastern group.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-RAS-13) From the Southern sub region group, Botswana and Namibia qualified for the Africa Regional Finals.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-BotNam-14)

The Regional Finals were held in Uganda in May 2019.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Uga19-15)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-16) Namibia and Kenya both progressed to the T20 World Cup Qualifier after finishing first and second respectively in the Regional Finals.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-17) In July 2019, the ICC suspended Zimbabwe Cricket, with the team barred from taking part in ICC events.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-18) As a result of their suspension, the ICC confirmed that Nigeria would replace them in the T20 World Cup Qualifier tournament.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-19)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
The **2018–19 ICC T20 World Cup Africa Qualifier** was a tournament played as part of qualification process for the 2021 ICC T20 World Cup.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-1)
Twelve regional qualifiers for the 2021 World Cup were held by the International Cricket Council (ICC), with 62 teams[[n 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Teams-2) competing during 2018 in five regions – Africa (3 groups), Americas (2), Asia (2), East Asia Pacific (2) and Europe (3). The top 25 sides from these progressed to five Regional Finals in 2019, with seven teams then going on to compete in the 2019 ICC T20 World Cup Qualifier,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-pressrelase-3)[[n 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-UAE=sr-4) along with the six lowest ranked sides from the ICC T20I Championship.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-pressrelase-3)
texts.1: The first African sub-regional qualifier (North-Western sub region) was held in Nigeria, with the two other groups staged in Botswana and Rwanda.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Road_to_2020-5)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Africa_sub_region-6) The top two teams in each group advanced to the regional finals tournament, which will determine two African entrants to the 2019 ICC T20 World Cup Qualifier. In April 2018, the International Cricket Council (ICC) granted full international status to Twenty20 men's matches played between member sides from 1 January 2019 onwards. Therefore, all the matches in the Regional Finals were played as Twenty20 Internationals (T20Is).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-status-7)
texts.2: From the North-Western sub region group, both Ghana and Nigeria qualified for the Africa Regional Finals.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-GhaNgr-8)Simon Ateak of Ghana was named the player of the tournament in the North-Western group.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-9) The second group, the Eastern sub region, started on 7 July 2018.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-10) Both Kenya and Uganda qualified for the Africa Regional Finals from the Eastern sub region group.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Kenya-11)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Uganda-12) Uganda's Riazat Ali Shah was named the player of the tournament for the Eastern group.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-RAS-13) From the Southern sub region group, Botswana and Namibia qualified for the Africa Regional Finals.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-BotNam-14)
texts.3:
The Regional Finals were held in Uganda in May 2019.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-Uga19-15)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-16) Namibia and Kenya both progressed to the T20 World Cup Qualifier after finishing first and second respectively in the Regional Finals.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-17) In July 2019, the ICC suspended Zimbabwe Cricket, with the team barred from taking part in ICC events.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-18) As a result of their suspension, the ICC confirmed that Nigeria would replace them in the T20 World Cup Qualifier tournament.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Men's_T20_World_Cup_Africa_qualifier#cite_note-19)
